references.text: The Lord speaks to Moses, a common introductory formula showing how God communicates His commands through Moses.
The Lord suddenly speaks to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, demonstrating God's direct communication with the leaders.
The Lord speaks to Moses and Aaron together, the same pattern of divine revelation to both leaders.
The Lord speaks to Moses and Aaron concerning judgment, a similar context where divine speech initiates an act of judgment.
The Lord speaks to Moses and Aaron, showing the established pattern from Exodus where God addresses both leaders.
The Lord speaks to Moses and Aaron in Egypt, an early example of God communicating with both leaders together.
The Lord speaks to Moses and Aaron, the same formula used repeatedly throughout Leviticus.
